text: Similarly, the 10 long-edge welding paths are marked with red lines in Figure 16b, and the long-edge welds start at the center of the floor (y = 0), with welds 1 to 5 moving along the positive direction of the y-axis and welds 6 to 10 moving along the negative direction of the y-axis, respectively. In summary, the simulation started with the welding and cooling of the short edges, followed by the long-edge welding and cooling. Note that a dwell time of one second was added to ensure sufficient melting at the start point of welding. The welding simulation steps are tabulated in Table 2. Table 2. Temperature contours of the 24 m diameter tank floor (a) at half of the short-edge welding time and (b) at half of the long-edge welding time. For the welding bead setup in the thermal profile model, elements within welds on the long edges are activated while the short edges are being welded. This setup was chosen to avoid the convergence issue in the residual stress analysis when reactivating the elements of the long edges [4]. Figure 17 presents the temperature contours of the 24 m diameter tank floor at half of the welding time for the short-edge welding and the long-edge welding, respectively, as well as the single weld contours. The peak temperature of the short and long welds ranges from 2900°C to 3300°C. 14 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 18 presents the constraints imposed in the 24 m diameter tank floor model for residual stress and distortion analysis. Two different symbols represent different constraint types used in the model. The bottom line is the plane of symmetry perpendicular to the x-axis. As shown in Figure 18, one fixed constraint (Ui = 0, URi = 0, i = 1,2,3), marked by a star symbol, is applied at one of the corners of the plates (x = 1,219 mm, y = 0). In addition, solid dots with limited constraint (U3 = 0, UR1 = UR2 = 0) are applied to all the other corners of the plates. Figure 18. Figures 19 and 20 respectively present the von Mises, longitudinal, and transverse stress contours of the 24 m diameter tank floor after completion of the short-edge and long-edge welding.
